parsed.title: Guard message mismatch
parsed.detail: The Turn contract box states the stop message is `→ Next: unit-lane requires manual input — cannot proceed`. However, the specific guard sections in DESIGN.md and RESEARCH.md use `→ Next: unit-lane (design step) requires manual input — cannot proceed` and `→ Next: unit-lane (research step) requires manual input — cannot proceed`. The SKILL.md guard section also omits the step context. This inconsistency violates the workflow axis's requirement for consistent gate/verdict vocabularies.

parsed.title: Guard message format violation
parsed.detail: The Turn contract box claims the stop message is `→ Next: unit-lane requires manual input — cannot proceed`. The 'Close the unit' section (Step 6) and 'Execute triaged steps' section use `→ Next:` followed by a command path (e.g., `→ Next: /execute-phase ...` or `→ Next: /review-change ...`). The guard message lacks the leading slash and command structure used elsewhere for navigation, creating a drift in the 'Next' block format.

parsed.title: Guard message inconsistency
parsed.detail: The DESIGN.md needs-input guard emits `→ Next: unit-lane (design step) requires manual input — cannot proceed`. This contradicts the SKILL.md Turn contract which specifies `→ Next: unit-lane requires manual input — cannot proceed` (no step context). The unit's own documents contradict each other on the exact string for the halt condition.

parsed.title: Guard message inconsistency
parsed.detail: The RESEARCH.md needs-input guard emits `→ Next: unit-lane (research step) requires manual input — cannot proceed`. This contradicts the SKILL.md Turn contract which specifies `→ Next: unit-lane requires manual input — cannot proceed`. The unit's own documents contradict each other on the exact string for the halt condition.
